meta.title: Vintage Vocoder — Free AU & VST3 for macOS and Linux | Ruminant Audio Works
meta.description: Sonicism Vintage Vocoder, restored from 2002. Eight oscillators, up to 64 analysis bands and MIDI control. Free AU/VST3 for Mac and VST3 for Linux ARM64 and x86-64.
nav.label: Primary navigation
hero.copy: The original Sonicism vocoder from 2002, brought back for modern Macs and Linux. Robot voices, singing synths and spectral mischief — with MIDI finally in charge of the oscillators.
hero.platform: macOS 12+ · Apple Silicon + Intel · Linux ARM64 + x86-64

facts.label: Vintage Vocoder at a glance
features.title: Give your sound another voice.
features.intro: Use speech, a drum loop or another audio source to shape a carrier. Build that carrier with the eight internal oscillators, play it with MIDI, or bring your own audio.
features.oscillators.title: Eight oscillators. Your hands on the sound.
features.oscillators.copy: Blend sine, saw, square and triangle waves. Set each oscillator’s pitch, level and tuning in NORM mode, or switch to MIDI and play the carrier from your keyboard or DAW.
features.midi.title: Play the vocoder.
features.midi.copy: MIDI mode brings velocity, sustain and pitch bend to the internal carrier. Enabled oscillators set the available polyphony; the modulation wheel moves the filter cutoffs.
features.spectral.title: Shape the spectrum.
features.spectral.copy: Choose from 1 to 64 analysis bands, set the frequency range and sculpt the result with the resonant filter. Blend dry and vocoded audio, then trim the final output.
features.presets.title: Start somewhere interesting.
features.presets.copy: Explore 30 factory presets, including the recovered originals and six Getting Started sounds. Save your own settings as named presets and come back to them later.
story.title: A little unfinished business.
story.p1: Vintage Vocoder was released by Sonicism in 2002 — a heady time for plug-in development. Its FFT-based vocoder grew out of Tom Taylor’s undergraduate thesis, then found its way into the robot voices and sound effects of Microsoft’s epic space adventure game, Freelancer.
story.p2: The code was eventually open sourced on SourceForge. Then life took over: an unrelated startup, followed by kids, left the project waiting.
story.p3: Nearly 25 years later, Tom returned to finish what he started — using the OG Vintage Vocoder code, with a cheeky assist from AI to level things up. The original character and interface live on, with MIDI finally in charge of the oscillators.
story.quote: It’s older code, but it checks out.

setup.title: Two signals. One new sound.
setup.intro: A vocoder uses a modulator to shape a carrier. Start with a voice as the modulator and the internal oscillators as the carrier.
setup.install.title: Install the plug-in
setup.install.copy: Quit your DAW. On macOS, run the installer for AU Music Effect and VST3. On Linux, extract the archive matching your system and copy the complete Vintage Vocoder FX.vst3 bundle into ~/.vst3/. Reopen your DAW and rescan plug-ins if needed.
setup.insert.title: Add it to an audio track
setup.insert.copy: Insert Vintage Vocoder FX on a vocal or another audio track. Choose NORM mode and play the track to hear the audio shape the fixed internal carrier. Keep the MIX control towards wet to hear the effect clearly.
setup.play.title: Put MIDI in charge
setup.play.copy: Switch to MIDI mode and route a MIDI track or keyboard to the effect. Play notes while the modulator audio runs. MIDI routing to audio effects depends on your DAW; both audio and MIDI are needed in this mode.
modes.title: Six ways in.
modes.intro: The MODE knob selects where the carrier and modulator come from.
modes.norm: Main audio shapes the fixed internal oscillators.
modes.midi: Main audio shapes the MIDI-played internal carrier.
modes.ext: Main audio is the modulator; the sidechain is the carrier. Both need audio.
modes.modl: Left input is the modulator; right input is the carrier.
modes.modr: Right input is the modulator; left input is the carrier.
setup.help: Need a hand with a control? Turn on the ? button beside the Sonicism badge and hover for help.
